messages:
Linh Nguyen: Heads up — we saw a handful of requests in prod where an ephemeral exchange returned a token scoped to a different project than the caller. Not sure if it's a bug or just unexpected UX.
Rashid Khan: Ugh. Can you paste an example trace id?
Linh Nguyen: trace=trc-9b3f. Hit via api-gateway, route: /v1/engines/generate, subject=service:ingest-worker. Token claims show project=proj-b-slug, origin=proj-a.
Evie Park: That sounds like a consent/exchange flow mishandling. Could be the consent bubble not being shown in console so users consent to the wrong project.
Matt O'Leary: Are we seeing authz check fail before invoke or after? If it failed, should be blocked. If allowed, router might be doing a fallback to a compatible key with looser scoping.
Linh Nguyen: Request succeeded and incurred billing under proj-b. So router selected a compatible SA token from the key cache. No explicit failure.
Rashid Khan: Hmm — routing policy currently prefers token affinity by key-id, then by tenant affinity, then fallback to 'compatible' tokens. That compatible fallback is the scary part.
Evie Park: UX idea: surface a consent bubble on exchange when project-scoped SA is about to be swapped to a different project. Small modal: "You're exchanging token X for project B — continue?" Would catch accidental cross-project exchanges.
Matt O'Leary: Love the mitigator. But we still need telemetry to detect when this happens automatically. Can we add a signal in request logs for "exchange_project_mismatch": true?
Linh Nguyen: I can add a light-weight flag in the auth-proxy log line. Example: `auth_proxy: exchange_project_mismatch=proj-a->proj-b token_id=sa_123`
ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: auth-proxy patch (canary) to mainland region at 2025-06-12T14:00Z by Rashid Khan :rocket:
Rashid Khan: Proposed short-term fix: disallow compatible fallback unless the caller explicitly opts in via a header `X-Allow-Project-Fallback: true`. Long-term: audit console flows and add consent UI.
Evie Park: For rollout UX, default should be off. Show a small banner in console where admins can opt-in org-wide and enable an audit trail checkbox.
Matt O'Leary: Query suggestion for telemetry (search events): 
```
SELECT timestamp, caller_project, issued_project, token_id
FROM auth_events
WHERE issued_project != caller_project
AND event_type = 'token_issue'
ORDER BY timestamp DESC
LIMIT 100;
```
Linh Nguyen: Good. I'll wire that into the per-route dashboard as a sample widget and heatmap.
Rashid Khan: One more nuance: billing attribution needs to be correct immediately. If fallback occurs, we should attribute cost to caller unless explicitly swapped by an admin. Otherwise orgs will get billed unexpectedly.
Evie Park: So policy update: attribution = caller_project by default; only change to issued_project if consent header present or console opt-in enabled.
Matt O'Leary: Sounds reasonable. Need SRE runbook: if we see >5 mismatches/minute, auto-roll back fallback behavior and open pager.
Linh Nguyen: I'll open a quick RFC and include the SQL, proposed header, console mock, and rollout playbook. Will ping infra and billing.
Rashid Khan: Thanks — tagging @Evie and @Matt for UX and billing review. :thumbsup:
Evie Park: Reviewing. Also let's add a sample in docs showing the safe exchange pattern with `X-Allow-Project-Fallback`.
Matt O'Leary: Agree. After canary, prod rollout in two phases: telemetry only -> header opt-in -> UI opt-in.
Linh Nguyen: OK. Created RFC draft: https://docs.internal/rfcs/consent-bubble-exchange (WIP).
